pr_summary: Fix MSAA rendering issue where multiple cameras sharing the same render target only show contributions from first and last camera. The fix changes the internal bookkeeping so that the active texture flag is stored per-target (keyed by normalized render target and HDR settings) rather than per-camera, ensuring all cameras rendering to the same target share a single piece of state for texture swapping.
environment_management: Rust toolchain managed by rustup. Project uses standard Cargo workspace structure. No special environment manager like conda, poetry, or npm required.
patch_file_cues: Changes tuple from (a, b, sampled) to (a, b, sampled, main_texture)
Moves main_texture AtomicUsize from per-entity to per-target cache entry
test_file_cues: Compile-fail tests in crates/bevy_ecs_compile_fail_tests and crates/bevy_reflect_compile_fail_tests
platform_constraint_evidence: Linux CI installs libasound2-dev, libudev-dev, libwayland-dev, libxkbcommon-dev
wgpu dependency supports Linux with Vulkan, DX12, Metal backends
Project is cross-platform Rust with no Windows/macOS-only code in touched files
notes: Bevy is a Rust game engine with a Cargo workspace structure. The fix modifies the prepare_view_targets function in bevy_render to fix MSAA texture swapping when multiple cameras share a render target. The project requires Rust 1.76.0+. CI runs on all three major platforms. Linux builds require ALSA, udev, Wayland, and xkbcommon development libraries. Tests can be run via 'cargo test' or the custom CI tool 'cargo run -p ci -- test'. The touched file is in the rendering subsystem and the fix is purely Rust code with no platform-specific dependencies.
